questions.stem: The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by which amendment, and where does it now stand?
options: 42nd Amendment; shifted to Article 31C
44th Amendment; made a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A
44th Amendment; retained as a Fundamental Right under Article 19
86th Amendment; shifted to Article 21A
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT included in the meaning of 'State' under Article 12 of the Constitution?
options: Local authorities such as municipalities and panchayats
A purely private company with no governmental control
State legislatures and Parliament
Statutory and government-controlled bodies like LIC and ONGC
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: With reference to Article 13, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: A constitutional amendment is not 'law' under Article 13, but can be struck down if it violates the basic structure
Constitutional amendments are always 'law' under Article 13 and can be struck down on that ground
Every law inconsistent with Fundamental Rights remains valid until repealed
Only pre-Constitution laws are tested against Fundamental Rights
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'Doctrine of Severability' associated with Article 13 means that
options: the entire law is void if any part violates Fundamental Rights
only the part of a law inconsistent with Fundamental Rights is struck down, the rest surviving if it can operate independently
a person may voluntarily waive his Fundamental Rights
a law once declared void can never be revived
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under Article 14, the expressions 'equality before law' and 'equal protection of the laws' are respectively of
options: American and British origin
French and American origin
British and American origin
British and French origin
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following provisions was added to allow reservation for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in employment and education?
options: 103rd Amendment, 2019
102nd Amendment, 2018
101st Amendment, 2016
93rd Amendment, 2005
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The abolition of untouchability under Article 17 is enforceable against
options: the State only
both the State and private individuals
private individuals only
neither, as it is only a directive
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: With reference to Article 18, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are 'titles' and violate Article 18
Military and academic distinctions are banned as titles
Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are not 'titles' but cannot be used as a prefix or suffix to one's name
Citizens may freely accept titles from foreign states
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT one of the six freedoms guaranteed under Article 19?
options: Freedom to form associations or unions
Freedom to reside and settle in any part of India
Freedom of speech and expression
Right to strike
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The protection against self-incrimination under Article 20(3) does NOT extend to
options: compulsory production of material objects, thumb impressions and specimen signatures
testimonial compulsion in a criminal case
statements that expose a person to a criminal charge
being compelled to be a witness against oneself in a criminal trial
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of Fundamental Rights CANNOT be suspended even during a National Emergency?
options: Articles 14 and 19
Articles 20 and 21
Articles 19 and 21
Articles 21 and 22
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Right to Privacy was declared a Fundamental Right, flowing from Article 21, in which case?
options: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Francis Coralie Mullin v. UT of Delhi (1981)
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 21A, which makes elementary education a Fundamental Right, was inserted by which amendment and covers which age group?
options: 93rd Amendment; 6 to 18 years
42nd Amendment; 6 to 14 years
44th Amendment; 0 to 6 years
86th Amendment; 6 to 14 years
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under Article 22, a person arrested under ordinary law must be produced before the nearest Magistrate within
options: 24 hours of arrest, excluding the time of journey
one week of arrest
48 hours including the time of journey
72 hours excluding the time of journey
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in
options: only factories and mines
all occupations, while barring adolescents (14-18) from certain hazardous occupations
factories, mines and railways only
only hazardous occupations
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under Article 25, the right to 'propagate' religion does NOT include
options: transmitting one's religious beliefs to others
the right of Sikhs to wear and carry kirpans
forcible conversion of another person
open declaration of one's faith
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Religious instruction is completely prohibited in which one of the following types of educational institutions under Article 28?
options: Institutions administered by the State but established under a trust
Institutions receiving aid from State funds, with the guardian's consent
Institutions merely recognised by the State
Institutions wholly maintained out of State funds
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about Article 29 is correct?
options: The expression 'section of citizens' includes majority groups as well
Its protection is restricted only to minorities
It is available to both citizens and foreigners
It allows denial of admission to State-aided institutions on grounds of language
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Why did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar call Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
options: Because it lists all the Fundamental Rights
Because it guarantees the right to directly move the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights
Because it allows Parliament to amend Fundamental Rights
Because it defines the term 'State'
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The writ that questions the legality of a person's claim to a public office is
options: Mandamus
Habeas Corpus
Quo Warranto
Prohibition
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following writs means "you may have the body"?
options: Habeas Corpus
Mandamus
Certiorari
Quo Warranto
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: According to B.R. Ambedkar, which one among the following Articles is the heart and soul of the Constitution of India?
options: Article 15
Article 21
Article 23
Article 32
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which among the following fundamental rights is/are available to non-citizens? 1. Freedom of speech 2. Protection against self-incrimination 3. Freedom of conscience 4. Non-discrimination in matters of employment. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
2 only
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following correctly describes the term 'State' as defined in Article 12 of the Constitution of India?
options: It refers only to the Government of India
It refers only to the Government of India and the Parliament of India
It refers only to the Government of India, Parliament, and the Governments and Legislatures of each State
It refers to the Government and Parliament of India, the Governments and Legislatures of each State, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following fundamental rights as enshrined in the Constitution of India belong only to the citizens? 1. Article 19 - freedom of speech 2. Article 21 - life and personal liberty 3. Article 15 - prohibition of discrimination 4. Article 16 - equality of opportunity. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
options: 1, 2 and 3
2, 3 and 4
1, 3 and 4
1 and 4 only
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: During a National Emergency, the enforcement of which Articles CANNOT be suspended, reflecting a safeguard added after 1978?
options: Articles 14 and 19
Articles 22 and 32
Articles 19 and 31
Articles 20 and 21
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The writ of Mandamus canNOT be issued against which one of the following?
options: The President of India or a State Governor
An inferior court refusing to perform a duty
A government department neglecting an official duty
A public corporation failing in a statutory duty
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under Article 33, the power to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces and police is vested in
options: the State Legislatures
Parliament
the President by proclamation
the Supreme Court
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (Article 32) from that of a High Court (Article 226)?
options: The Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction is wider as it covers all legal rights
A High Court can issue writs only for Fundamental Rights, like the Supreme Court
The High Court's writ jurisdiction is wider, covering both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights, and it has discretion to refuse
Both can refuse to exercise writ jurisdiction at their discretion
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are
options: completely immune from judicial review
open to challenge only in the Supreme Court, not High Courts
automatically void
open to judicial review if they violate the basic structure of the Constitution
questions.subject: Polity
